reigns.note: No mythic king-list or named founder in the seven lenses — only Heracles' cattle-drive passage, where a bull broke away at Rhegium, swam to Sicily, and gave Italy its name (Tyrrhenian italus). Ovid names the opposite walls of Rhegium as strait geography (Met. 14.1–108), not a civic dynasty. Pausanias' Anaxilas (tyrant, Messenian Alcidamidas line) is historical colony-era and omitted. Scylla and Charybdis belong to the strait (Homer Od. 12), not to Rhegium's city sky.
